entries.title: Connect HubSpot from the HubSpot marketplace, write engagement back to HubSpot, and see accurate connection health
entries.summary: Three improvements to the HubSpot app: (1) Installs that start inside the HubSpot marketplace now land on a **Connect Sessionboard** claim page where you pick the organization to link — expired or already-claimed installs show a clear error. (2) **CRM → Connections → HubSpot** gains a **Write back** panel: choose which engagement data (properties and timeline events) Sessionboard pushes to HubSpot contact records; activity write-back is marked **Preview** until HubSpot approves the app's timeline events. (3) The connection health badge on every connected app now correctly shows **Connected**, **Reconnect needed**, or **Needs attention** instead of a raw object key.
entries.use_case: Teams that manage speaker and attendee relationships in HubSpot can now install the Sessionboard app directly from the HubSpot marketplace and immediately see engagement data written back to HubSpot contact records, keeping both systems in sync without manual exports.

cs_action.note: Activity (timeline events) write-back is preview-only until HubSpot approves the app's timeline events and the connection has the required OAuth grant. Do not promise full timeline write-back to customers yet.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to install the HubSpot app from the HubSpot marketplace, or wants engagement data to appear on HubSpot contact records automatically.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Sessionboard CRM who also use HubSpot for sales or marketing and want bidirectional data flow.
internal.gotchas: Timeline event (activity) write-back is gated behind both HubSpot app approval and the connection holding the timeline.write OAuth scope; the UI shows a preview-only notice until both conditions are met. The health badge fix affects all connected apps, not just HubSpot.
internal.talk_track: You can now install the Sessionboard HubSpot app straight from the HubSpot marketplace and have engagement data written back to your HubSpot contacts automatically — no manual exports needed.

draft.docs_gap: The article index has no dedicated HubSpot integration guide; a new guide under /apps/hubspot-integration should cover installing from HubSpot, the claim page flow, configuring write-back, and the health badge states.
draft.why_use_it: The HubSpot connection lets you install Sessionboard from either side — the Sessionboard app marketplace or the HubSpot marketplace — and keeps your HubSpot contact records enriched with the engagement data Sessionboard collects. Write-back pushes properties and timeline events to HubSpot automatically, so your sales and marketing teams see speaker and attendee activity without leaving HubSpot.

entries.title: HubSpot write-back screen and contact card matching by email
entries.summary: The **Write back** button now appears on HubSpot connections in the CRM app list, and the write-back configuration screen correctly loads HubSpot's toggles, Sessionboard-owned properties, and lists. The HubSpot contact card also matches people imported without a HubSpot link when their **email address** is provided, so contacts found by email are surfaced alongside those matched by HubSpot ID. Timeline-event write-back is shown as unavailable until HubSpot approves the app.
entries.use_case: Organizations using HubSpot as their CRM can now open the write-back configuration screen without errors and see exactly which Sessionboard properties and lists will be written back. Contacts imported into Sessionboard without a HubSpot link are now matched and surfaced on the HubSpot card when their email address is known, reducing gaps in the contact view.

cs_action.note: Timeline events (HubSpot activity) are disabled until HubSpot approves the app's event types; the screen will show timeline_available: false. Do not promise timeline write-back to customers yet.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a HubSpot customer asks about writing engagement back to HubSpot or reports that the Write back button was missing or the screen errored.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer with a HubSpot connection in Sessionboard CRM who wants to sync engagement data back to HubSpot contacts.
internal.gotchas: Timeline events are gated behind a server env var (HUBSPOT_APP_EVENTS_ENABLED) that defaults to off; the screen will report timeline_available: false and activity runs will be refused until HubSpot approves the account. Card matching by email is additive — requests without an email behave as before.
internal.talk_track: HubSpot customers can now open the write-back screen and configure which Sessionboard data flows into HubSpot. Contacts matched only by email — not a HubSpot ID — are now surfaced on the card too.

draft.docs_gap: The write-back guide should add a HubSpot-specific section covering the available toggles (suggestion, lists, Sessionboard-owned properties), the timeline-events availability indicator, and how contact card matching by email works.
draft.why_use_it: Write-back lets Sessionboard push engagement data — session participation, list membership and Sessionboard-owned properties — directly into HubSpot so your CRM stays current without manual exports. The configuration screen shows which toggles are active, what will be written, and whether timeline events are available, giving you full visibility before any data moves.
problems: src/data/release-notes/2026-11-11.json [hubspot-writeback-and-card-matching] article /sessionboard-crm/ams/write-back is in a self-serve suite — set "product" to that suite, or link a Platform guide

entries.title: CRM member value card and speaker finder now match speakers who exist only as Contacts
entries.summary: The **Member Value** card and the **Speaker Finder** in the CRM now recognise speakers who have a Contact record but no separate People row. Previously, those speakers returned no match on the card and were absent from finder results. Talks, award entries and draft submissions linked to a Contact-only speaker now appear correctly, and the speaker finder includes them as candidates alongside speakers who have full People records.

where.path: CRM → People → Member Value card / Speaker Finder

entries.use_case: An association using the Salesforce or HubSpot CRM package whose speakers are stored as Contacts (not People) will now see accurate talk counts and engagement data on the Member Value card, and the Speaker Finder will surface those speakers as recommendations instead of returning an empty list.

cs_action.note: Fix ships automatically; no configuration needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that the Speaker Finder returns zero results or that the Member Value card shows 'matched: false' for known speakers — especially on Platform orgs using Salesforce, HubSpot or Dynamics.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any CRM customer whose speakers are created as Contacts rather than People rows, which is the default for Platform organisations.
internal.staff_path: CRM → People → open a person → Member Value card; or CRM → Speaker Finder
internal.gotchas: Signals, credits, suggestions and membership data still require a People row and will be blank for Contact-only speakers — this is intentional. When a Contact-only speaker is suggested via the finder's suggest endpoint, a People row is created automatically.
internal.talk_track: If your Speaker Finder was coming back empty or your Member Value cards were all showing no match, this fix resolves it — speakers who live only as Contacts are now recognised correctly.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document that the CRM resolves speakers by Contact when no People row exists, and note which data (talks, award entries, drafts) is available for Contact-only speakers versus which (signals, credits, membership) requires a People row.
draft.why_use_it: The CRM's Speaker Finder and Member Value card help you identify your most engaged speakers and understand how deeply a member participates in your events. Use them to prioritise outreach, build speaker shortlists, and demonstrate member value to your board — all without leaving Sessionboard.

entries.title: Product-coloured sidebar tiles and page accents for all Platform users
entries.summary: The sidebar now shows a coloured tile for each module: **Program** green, **CRM** cyan, **Marketing** violet, **Learning** amber, **Awards** rose. The active row, the page-header icon tile and a soft colour wash at the top of the page follow whichever module you are in. Cards also have slightly rounder corners in both light and dark mode. Names, routes and layouts are unchanged.
entries.use_case: Teams working across multiple modules can instantly see which module they are in from the sidebar colour and the page-header accent, reducing navigation errors when switching between Program, CRM, Marketing and other areas.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer who asks about the new colours in the sidebar or notices the UI looks different after the 2026-11-11 release.
internal.who_should_get_it: All Platform users — no action needed, it is on by default.
internal.staff_path: Super-users can append ?accents=off to any URL to see the pre-accent look for Help Center screenshot work.
internal.gotchas: Help Center screenshots and training videos still show the old look until they are re-shot (estimated 500–800 screenshots and 76 training chapters). The ?accents=off override is staff-only and is ignored for customer accounts.
internal.talk_track: The sidebar now uses a distinct colour for each module — green for Program, cyan for CRM, violet for Marketing, amber for Learning, rose for Awards — so your team always knows at a glance where they are.

draft.docs_gap: The sidebar guide should add a section describing the module colour system (tile colours per module, active-row accent, page-header wash) and note that the look applies in both light and dark mode.
draft.why_use_it: The sidebar gives you a single place to move between every Sessionboard module. Product-coloured tiles and page accents make it immediately clear which module you are working in, so context-switching across Program, CRM, Marketing, Learning and Awards is faster and less error-prone. The colour system follows WCAG contrast requirements in both light and dark mode, so it works for every member of your team.

entries.title: CE Broker roster dates now match the provider's local time zone
entries.summary: The CE Broker CSV roster, XML file and file name now format completion dates in the organization's configured time zone instead of UTC. A learner who completes a course at 4:56 pm Pacific time on November 8 will appear as **11/08/2026** in the downloaded roster, matching the date shown on the **Credits** page.

where.path: Credits → CE Broker reporting → Download CSV

entries.use_case: A nursing association in a US time zone submits CE Broker rosters to a state board. Previously, a completion recorded late in the day could appear as the next calendar date in the exported file, creating a discrepancy that could fail a compliance check. The roster now shows the same date the admin sees on screen.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that completion dates in their CE Broker CSV or XML roster are one day off from what the Credits page shows.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organization using CE Broker reporting, especially those in time zones significantly behind UTC (US Pacific, Mountain, Central, Eastern) where late-day completions were most likely to shift to the next UTC date.
internal.staff_path: Credits → CE Broker reporting → Download CSV
internal.gotchas: The fix reads the organization's timezone field. If an organization has no timezone configured, dates fall back to UTC — same as before. Confirm the org timezone is set correctly if a customer still sees a mismatch.
internal.talk_track: The date on your CE Broker roster now matches the date you see on the Credits page, so your state-board submissions will reflect the correct completion day.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that completion dates in the downloaded CSV and XML roster are formatted in the organization's configured time zone, and that the date will match what is shown on the Credits page.

entries.title: Site sign-in links show "Continue as <email>" before opening the portal
entries.summary: Every sign-in link on a Sessionboard Site — including Program Sites and Awards Sites — now shows a **Continue as <email>** confirmation screen before granting access. If the link has expired, the page offers **Send a new link** so the person can get a fresh one without contacting the organizer.

where.path: Any Site sign-in link (speaker portal, review portal, Awards site, Program site)

entries.use_case: Prevents a shared or forwarded magic link from silently signing in the wrong person, and lets anyone with an expired link request a new one on the spot instead of emailing support.

cs_action.note: Every reviewer, submitter and speaker who opens a Site sign-in link now sees one extra screen. No action needed to enable it, but customers should be aware so they don't get support tickets about the new screen.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer who uses magic-link sign-in for portals, review portals or Awards/Program sites — especially before a review cycle or portal launch.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers; this is on by default for every Site sign-in link.
internal.gotchas: This is a breaking change noted in the PR: every customer's reviewers and submitters see the extra confirmation screen. Customers who relied on links opening instantly may ask about it.
internal.talk_track: When someone opens their portal link, they now see a quick confirmation screen showing which email address they are signing in as. If their link has expired, they can request a new one right there.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the new "Continue as <email>" confirmation screen and the "Send a new link" expired-link flow for magic-link sign-in.
draft.why_use_it: Magic links are convenient, but they can be forwarded or opened on the wrong device. The confirmation screen lets the person verify they are signing in as the right account before the portal opens. If the link has already expired, they can request a fresh one immediately without contacting the organizer.

entries.title: Time quizzes, draw from a question bank, and score written answers in the course builder
entries.summary: Three new course-builder capabilities are now available in Sessionboard Learning. **Timed quizzes**: set a **Time limit** (minutes) on any quiz; the server holds the deadline so reloading never resets the clock, and a late submit scores as zero. **Extra time**: grant a learner a per-quiz accommodation under **Learner accommodations** so the timer extends for that person only. **Question bank**: save questions to a shared bank, tag them, and add a **Bank draw** block to a quiz that pulls a random set by tag — question IDs stay stable across republishes. **Score written answers**: open **Approvals → Answers to score** to review free-text and file responses, leave comments, and approve or reject each attempt; the learner sees the result on their quiz card.

where.path: Learning → Courses → [course] → [lesson] → Quiz settings / Approvals → Answers to score / Learning → Question bank

entries.use_case: A certification body running a proctored online exam can set a 90-minute time limit so learners cannot take unlimited time, grant extra time to registered accommodations, pull a unique randomised question set per attempt from a shared bank, and then manually score essay answers before credit is awarded.

cs_action.note: All three capabilities are additive: a time limit only applies when an author sets it, the bank is only used when an author adds a bank_draw block, and answer scoring only appears for quiz types that already waited for review. Nothing changes for existing courses.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about timed assessments, randomised question pools, or manual grading of open-ended quiz answers in Learning.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Sessionboard Learning for certification or compliance training who need exam-grade controls.
internal.staff_path: Learning → Courses → [course] → [lesson] → Quiz settings (time limit); Learning → Question bank (bank management); Learning → Approvals → Answers to score (review queue)
internal.gotchas: Time limits are server-enforced; reloading the page does not reset the clock. A late submit is automatically scored zero. Extra time is set per learner per quiz under Learner accommodations — it does not apply globally.
internal.talk_track: You can now run a real timed exam inside your learning site, pull a different random question set for each learner from your question bank, and manually review and score essay or file answers before credit is granted.

draft.docs_gap: The /sessionboard-learning/courses/timed-quizzes guide should document how to set a time limit on a quiz, how the server-side timer works (no reset on reload, late-submit scores as zero), and how to grant per-learner extra time via Learner accommodations. The /sessionboard-learning/courses/question-bank guide should cover adding questions to the bank, tagging them, and inserting a Bank draw block. The /sessionboard-learning/courses/score-written-answers guide should explain the Approvals → Answers to score queue, the review POST with comments, and what the learner sees after scoring.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Learning's course builder lets you create structured, assessable courses directly from your event content. Timed quizzes enforce exam conditions without any third-party tool. The question bank lets your team build a library of reusable, tagged questions and draw randomised subsets so each learner sees a different set. Scoring written and file answers gives instructors a review queue where they can read responses, leave comments, and approve or reject attempts before credit is recorded.

entries.title: Run an awards program without a Platform contract
entries.summary: Sessionboard Awards is now available as a self-serve product at **/awards**, in the same workspace as Marketing and Learning. Organizers can sign up, create programs, manage categories, collect nominations, run one review pass, pick winners and announce results — all without a Platform event. A second review round, entry fees/payments, SSO and a named CSM are locked to **Enterprise Awards** and show an upgrade prompt on self-serve plans.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Awards self-serve sign-up

entries.use_case: Associations and event teams that run annual awards programs can now sign up for Sessionboard Awards directly, set up categories and a nomination form, invite reviewers, and announce winners — without needing a full Platform contract. Teams that need multiple review rounds, entry fees or SSO can upgrade to Enterprise Awards.

cs_action.note: Sign-up is behind the AWARDS_SIGNUP_ENABLED flag and Stripe sandbox products (awd_* lookup keys) plus the Awards billing portal config are not yet created — Checkout cannot complete until those are provisioned. Do not promote self-serve sign-up to customers until the flag is enabled and Stripe is configured.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a prospect or existing customer asks about running an awards or recognition program independently of their Platform events, or when they are evaluating standalone awards tools.
internal.who_should_get_it: Associations, professional societies and event teams that run annual awards, recognition or grant programs and want a self-serve option without a full Platform contract.
internal.staff_path: /awards/:orgId — visible once AWARDS_SIGNUP_ENABLED is on and Stripe products are provisioned.
internal.gotchas: Self-serve plan is limited to one review round; a second round, entry fees/payments, SSO and a named CSM require Enterprise Awards. The API, Public API and MCP return 403 enterprise_only for those features on a self-serve plan. Stripe sandbox products and billing portal config for Awards are not yet created — Checkout will fail until they are set up.
internal.talk_track: You can now sign up for Sessionboard Awards directly and run your full awards program — nomination form, reviewer scoring and winner announcement — without a Platform contract. If you need multiple review rounds or entry fees, Enterprise Awards has you covered.

draft.docs_gap: The get-started guide should document the self-serve sign-up flow, the workspace URL (/awards), the distinction between self-serve and Enterprise Awards features (second review round, payments, SSO, CSM), and the upgrade path from within the Awards workspace.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Awards gives you a dedicated workspace to run the full lifecycle of an awards program: build a branded nomination form, collect and manage submissions, assign reviewers, score entries and announce winners. It keeps every program in one place so your team always knows where nominations stand and reviewers always know what to score next. Enterprise Awards adds a second review round, entry fees and payments, SSO and a dedicated CSM for organisations that need them.

entries.title: Grant API tokens CRM read and write access
entries.summary: The API token dialog's **Opt-in** section now includes two new checkboxes: **CRM (read)** (`read:crm`) and **CRM (write)** `write:crm`. Tick either or both when creating a token to allow integrations — such as the Salesforce, HubSpot and Dynamics apps — to read CRM data or perform actions like accepting and dismissing records. Neither scope is included in the default, **All**, or **Read** presets; they must be explicitly selected.

enable.path: Settings → API Tokens → New Token → Opt-in scopes

where.path: Settings → API Tokens → New Token → Opt-in scopes

entries.use_case: Organizations using the Salesforce, HubSpot or Dynamics apps can now issue tokens that carry CRM scopes, enabling those integrations to both read CRM data and take actions such as accepting or dismissing records — something that was not possible before.

cs_action.note: Customers using the Salesforce, HubSpot or Dynamics apps who previously could not Accept or Dismiss records via the API should regenerate their Named Credential token with the write:crm scope ticked.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that their Salesforce or HubSpot integration can read CRM data but cannot accept or dismiss records, or asks why CRM actions fail with a 400 error.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organization using the Salesforce, HubSpot or Dynamics app connections, or any customer building a custom integration against the /v1/crm/ API endpoints.
internal.staff_path: Settings → API Tokens → New Token → Opt-in scopes → CRM (read) / CRM (write)
internal.gotchas: These scopes are never added automatically — the token creator must tick them explicitly. Tokens created before this change do not gain the scopes retroactively; a new token must be issued.
internal.talk_track: You can now issue an API token that lets your Salesforce or HubSpot integration both read and write to the CRM — including accepting and dismissing records — without giving it broader access than it needs.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the CRM (read) and CRM (write) opt-in scopes, explain what each allows against the /v1/crm/ endpoints, and note that they are required for Salesforce, HubSpot and Dynamics app Named Credentials to perform write actions.
draft.why_use_it: API tokens let you connect external tools and integrations to Sessionboard without sharing your login credentials. Opt-in scopes give you fine-grained control over exactly what each token can access, so a token issued to a CRM integration carries only the permissions it needs and nothing more.

entries.title: API tokens can now carry read:crm and write:crm scopes
entries.summary: Organization API tokens can now be issued with **read:crm** and **write:crm** scopes, giving external systems — such as a Salesforce Named Credential — authenticated access to CRM routes. Previously, only legacy keyless tokens could reach those endpoints; any scoped key received a 403.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → CRM scopes; then generate a token via POST …/api-tokens with read:crm or write:crm

entries.use_case: A team connecting Salesforce (or any external system) to Sessionboard via an org API key can now grant that key explicit CRM read or write access, so it can accept speakers, dismiss records, and run CRM actions without needing a legacy unscoped token.

cs_action.note: The UI token picker does not yet list read:crm or write:crm — scopes must be set via the API (POST …/api-tokens). Customers need to know this before attempting to configure the Salesforce package.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer is setting up the Salesforce integration or any external system that calls /v1/crm/* routes with an org API key and is hitting 403 errors.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Salesforce package (lennd/sessionboard-salesforce) or any integration that reads or writes CRM data via the public API.
internal.staff_path: Organization → Settings → API Tokens (token creation via API only for now; web UI picker does not yet surface these scopes)
internal.gotchas: The web-ui-v2 token picker does not list read:crm or write:crm yet — they must be added programmatically. New tokens never include these scopes by default; they must be set explicitly.
internal.talk_track: Your Salesforce connection can now use a properly scoped org API key to read and write CRM data, instead of relying on a legacy unscoped token.

draft.docs_gap: The Authentication guide's Token Scopes section should list read:crm and write:crm, note they are Preview-gated, and explain that they must currently be set via the API rather than the token picker UI.
draft.why_use_it: API tokens let external systems authenticate with Sessionboard using tightly scoped credentials. By choosing exactly which scopes a token carries — such as read:crm or write:crm — you limit what a compromised key can reach while still giving integrations like Salesforce Named Credentials the access they need to read contacts and trigger CRM actions.

entries.title: Choose which Marketing capabilities appear in your workspace with "Add to Marketing"
entries.summary: A new **Add to Marketing** catalog lets organizers add or remove individual Marketing capabilities — such as Clips, Posts or Dispatch — from their workspace. The sidebar, mobile nav, **Ask** home, the **Ask** drawer, Goals' ads lane and Pages' gallery card all update to reflect the active set. During sign-up, a **"What brings you here?"** focus question tailors the initial view to the chosen goal.
entries.use_case: An event team that only uses Clips and Dispatch can hide Posts, Quotes and other capabilities they don't need, keeping the Marketing workspace focused on their actual workflow. A new workspace member answering "What brings you here?" during sign-up sees only the tools relevant to their goal from day one.

cs_action.note: The catalog is on by default for all Marketing (beta) workspaces. Verify the customer's capability set looks correct after the web-api round-8 deploy; an older API causes the catalog read to fail silently (nothing is hidden).

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Marketing customer says the workspace feels cluttered or they can't find the tools they use most, or when onboarding a new Marketing workspace.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any team using Sessionboard Marketing (beta) who wants a focused workspace; especially useful for smaller teams with a single content goal.
internal.gotchas: Requires web-api round 8 to be deployed first. If the API is older, the catalog read fails and nothing is hidden — safe but the feature won't appear. The focus key in sign-up also requires the new setup schema; an older API rejects it. Capability set is stored in Organizations.metadata.marketing_capabilities.
internal.talk_track: You can now pick exactly which Marketing tools show up in your workspace — add Clips and Dispatch, hide what you don't use, and the sidebar, Ask and your Goals page all update instantly.

draft.docs_gap: The get-started guide should add a section explaining the Add to Marketing catalog: how to open it, add or remove a capability, and how the sidebar and Ask home reflect the active set.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Marketing brings together content creation, distribution and event promotion in one workspace. The Add to Marketing catalog lets you decide which capabilities — Clips, Posts, Dispatch, Advocacy and more — appear in your sidebar and throughout the workspace, so your team sees only the tools they actually use. The focus question at sign-up means new members start with a workspace shaped around their goal rather than every available feature.

entries.title: Marketing workspaces track the capabilities they use
entries.summary: A self-serve Marketing workspace now maintains a **Capability catalog** — the set of Marketing features the workspace actively uses. The catalog starts from the answers given at sign-up (including the new **Focus** question) and grows automatically as capabilities are used. Organizers can view, add and remove capabilities from the catalog, and each change is recorded in the organization's history.
entries.use_case: A marketing team that only uses Clips and Advocacy can keep their workspace focused on those tools; the catalog surfaces the right defaults and guidance without surfacing unrelated features. As the team adopts new capabilities, the catalog updates automatically so their lifecycle guidance stays relevant.

cs_action.note: The capability set is seeded from sign-up answers including the new 'focus' field. Existing workspaces with no set will receive a general starter set. Review with customers before discussing lifecycle guidance that references the catalog.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When onboarding a new Marketing workspace or when a customer asks why certain features or guidance appear in their workspace.
internal.who_should_get_it: All self-serve Marketing workspace customers, especially new sign-ups who answer the Focus question during setup.
internal.gotchas: The sign-up 'focus' key requires the new API schema; an older API will reject it. The capability set lives in Organizations.metadata.marketing_capabilities — no migration runs for existing workspaces, so they start from the general starter set. Help Center docs for this feature deploy separately after this release.
internal.talk_track: Your Marketing workspace now tracks which tools your team actually uses, so the guidance and playbooks you see are tailored to your workflow rather than every feature in the product.

draft.docs_gap: The get-started guide should add a section explaining the Capability catalog: what it is, how it is seeded from sign-up answers, how it grows automatically, and how organizers can view or edit it.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Marketing covers a wide range of content and distribution tools, and not every team uses all of them. The capability catalog lets a workspace declare which tools it relies on, so setup guidance, playbooks and lifecycle prompts stay focused on what the team actually does. The catalog grows on its own as new tools are adopted, keeping it accurate without manual upkeep.

entries.title: Connect HubSpot directly from the HubSpot Marketplace and sync speaker activity back to contacts
entries.summary: The Sessionboard HubSpot app now supports three new capabilities. **Install from HubSpot**: clicking **Install** in the HubSpot Marketplace starts an OAuth flow that links a HubSpot portal to a Sessionboard org — no manual token entry required. **Timeline events**: speaker activity (Spoke, Reviewed, CE credit, Award entry, Attended) is written back to the matching HubSpot contact's timeline automatically; each activity is deduplicated by its Sessionboard key. **Suggestions**: five `sessionboard_suggested_*` contact properties and one static HubSpot list per topic are created and kept current from each contact's top open speaker suggestion.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable the HubSpot app; then Apps → HubSpot

entries.use_case: An association that tracks speaker prospects in HubSpot can install the Sessionboard app directly from the HubSpot Marketplace, then see every speaking, reviewing and attendance activity appear on the HubSpot contact timeline — and have HubSpot lists automatically populated with contacts suggested as next speakers by topic.

cs_action.note: Timeline events and the HubSpot CRM card/workflow action are not yet verified live via OAuth install — only the suggestion and property-write paths have been confirmed on a test portal. Card and workflow-action endpoints need the app uploaded and installed by OAuth before they can be tested. Region routing (EU, ME) is also a follow-up. Do not broadly announce until the OAuth install path is confirmed end-to-end.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer uses HubSpot as their CRM and wants speaker engagement data or next-speaker suggestions to appear there automatically.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with an active HubSpot connection who manage speaker pipelines or prospect outreach in HubSpot.
internal.staff_path: Apps → HubSpot (org level); OAuth install also reachable from the HubSpot Marketplace.
internal.gotchas: Timeline write-back is blocked when the connection uses a private-app token or was not granted the `timeline` HubSpot scope. The CRM card and workflow action (invite-to-speak) return fixture/FAIL_CONTINUE responses until the Salesforce track ships the underlying module. Portal 657654 is hard-blocked. Region routing for EU and ME is not yet built.
internal.talk_track: Your HubSpot contacts will automatically show every session your speakers have presented, reviewed or attended, and you'll get a HubSpot list of suggested next speakers for each topic — all without leaving HubSpot.

draft.docs_gap: The App Marketplace guide should add a dedicated HubSpot section covering the Marketplace install flow, the OAuth scopes required, how timeline events are written back, and how the suggested-speaker contact properties and lists work.
draft.why_use_it: The HubSpot app keeps your speaker and session data in sync with your CRM without manual exports. Speaker activity — sessions presented, reviews completed, credits earned, awards entered and events attended — flows back to HubSpot contact timelines so your team always has a full engagement picture. Suggested-speaker properties and topic lists let you act on Sessionboard's recommendations directly inside HubSpot workflows and views.

entries.title: Attach files to reviewer messages on Review plan Sites
entries.summary: Reviewers on a Review plan Site can now attach files (CSV, JPG, PDF, and other allowed types) to messages on a submission without seeing "The upload didn't finish. Try again." Files with non-ASCII names (e.g. **Résumé.pdf**) also upload and download correctly. The same fix applies to Awards / Interest Form file questions on Sites, Academy task hand-ins, course reading documents, and caption uploads.

where.path: Review portal → submission → Messages → attach a file

entries.use_case: A reviewer trying to attach supporting evidence or a marked-up PDF to a submission message can now complete the upload without error, including files with accented or non-Latin characters in the filename.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A reviewer or organizer reports that file attachments on submission messages fail with 'The upload didn't finish. Try again.' — this is now resolved in production.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Review plan Sites where reviewers attach files to submission messages, or using Awards / Interest Form file questions, Academy task hand-ins, or course documents.
internal.staff_path: Review portal (the Site) → open a submission → Messages → attach a file
internal.gotchas: API-only fix (web-api #5279, released 2026-11-10): the portal now sends only the headers the upload is signed for. Blocked file types (.exe, .svg) are still refused. No attachment had uploaded in production before the fix, so there is nothing to reconcile.
internal.talk_track: Reviewers can now reliably attach files — including those with accented or non-Latin filenames — to messages on any submission in a Review plan Site.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that reviewers can attach files to messages on a submission and list the supported file types and size limits for that context.
